sections.h2: What does a quick New Braunfels sale involve?
sections.html:
A direct cash sale here can close on your calendar, often in a few weeks, since no lender signs off on the buyer. You give up some price in exchange for speed and certainty, so measure the offer against a listing estimate before you decide.

The city has been one of the fastest growing places in Texas. Census QuickFacts puts the 2025 population estimate at 122,492, a 35.5 percent rise above the 2020 base. Rapid growth brings many new neighbors and many new listings, so a tired house competes with newer builds.

Typical reasons owners choose a quick sale:

  • Relocation along the I-35 corridor toward Austin or San Antonio.
  • An older home with repairs that financed buyers will not accept.
  • A short-term or vacation rental that no longer pays off.
  • An inherited house shared among several heirs.
  • A property with a code, title or tax problem.

sections.h2: How does New Braunfels work as a place to sell?
sections.html:
New Braunfels is the seat of Comal County, at the meeting of the Guadalupe and Comal rivers and Interstate 35 and Farm Road 725, thirty miles northeast of San Antonio and forty-five miles southwest of Austin, per the Handbook of Texas. The same entry says the city extends into Guadalupe County, so some parcels belong to a different county than the one the name suggests.

German immigrants founded the town on March 21, 1845. Its economy grew from mills, manufacturing and a commercial center, and later tourism: Landa Park, the rivers, Canyon Lake after 1964, Natural Bridge Caverns and Wurstfest. Those draws keep short stays and second homes in the market.

The Handbook also notes that the city is in the San Antonio metropolitan area, which is why many owners commute or sell to buyers moving from there.

sections.h2: How do New Braunfels values compare with smaller Texas towns?
sections.html:
Values here run well above the state's small-city markets. The table below shows what Census QuickFacts reports for 2020 to 2024 except where a row says otherwise.

Mortgage holders pay a median $2,088 monthly, and 83.7 percent of residents stayed at the same address through the prior year. A stable, owner-heavy base like this means buyers have choices, and a visibly worn house is easy to skip.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district and tax rules apply?
sections.html:
For Comal County parcels, the Comal Appraisal District values the property and handles exemptions. Its office is at 900 S. Seguin Ave., New Braunfels, open weekdays, and its site highlights April 15 and May 15 as key dates. If your parcel lies in Guadalupe County, ask the tax office there who appraises it.

The state rules are on the Comptroller's site. Homeowners get a school district exemption of $140,000, and a homestead's appraised value cannot rise more than 10 percent a year once the exemption has been in place, effective from the January 1 after it first applies. School taxes can be frozen for senior and disabled owners.

  • Value date: January 1.
  • Protest deadline: mid-May in most cases.
  • Delinquency: February 1 after a January 31 deadline.

The cap helps long-term owners but resets for a buyer, so a recent sale can raise the bill for the next owner. That is useful to mention when you talk price.

sections.h2: Can I use a short-term rental or a rented house as a seller?
sections.html:
New Braunfels is known for river and lake visitors, so many houses have served as short stays. If yours is rented, the tenant's rights come first in the timeline. In Texas, a landlord generally gives at least three days' written notice to vacate unless the lease says otherwise, then files in justice court if the tenant stays, per the State Law Library.

Ask the City of New Braunfels about any permit or registration tied to a short-term rental before you transfer the property, since requirements can differ from one address to another. Any investor buying it will want to know the rental history and any open compliance issue.

sections.h2: What if the house has a mortgage default or tax lien?
sections.html:
Act early. The State Law Library says a borrower has 20 days after the notice of default to cure it, and a posted sale notice follows at least three weeks before the auction. Auction day is the first Tuesday of each month, in the area set by the commissioners court.

Tax liens run on their own track. Each January 1 one attaches, and after February 1 penalties and interest build up, with an added collection penalty of up to 20 percent if the unit hires a private attorney. Both payoffs are deducted at closing, so get the exact numbers from the title company.

sections.h2: How have growth and commuting shaped New Braunfels neighborhoods?
sections.html:
The city has repeatedly absorbed new land. The Handbook records that New Braunfels incorporated eight suburbs in 1947 and by 1990 reached into Guadalupe County, and its population went from 36,494 in 2000 to 90,403 in the 2020 Census. Land area was 45.18 square miles in 2020, up from 43.87 in 2010, and density rose from 1,316 to 2,001 people per square mile.

Workers average 27.1 minutes on the road, which is longer than in smaller Texas towns, and 98.0 percent of households have a computer. Those commuters often want a move-in-ready house near I-35 or Farm Road 725, so a home that needs updates may do better with an investor than with a typical family buyer.

Older neighborhoods near Landa Park and the river carry the city's German-era history, while newer subdivisions on the edge follow the growth. Tell any buyer which category your street falls in and whether your lot has flood or drainage history, since the rivers shape much of the town.

sections.h2: Which fast-sale option fits a New Braunfels owner?
sections.html:
The right path depends on condition and timing. A cash offer fits a place that needs repairs or an owner with a firm deadline, while a listing may net more for a polished house in a strong subdivision.

  • Cash offer: no repairs, owner picks the date, no financing contingency.
  • Traditional listing: higher potential price, plus commissions, repairs and showings.
  • Sale to an heir or relative: may need a deed and clear title paperwork.

Ask each buyer for a written offer and compare the net you would keep after payoffs and fees.

sections.h2: How does closing and recording work?
sections.html:
The title company prepares the deed and settlement statement, and the county clerk where the property sits files the deed. A deed needs a notarized or otherwise officially acknowledged signature before it can be recorded.

The County Clerk Manual sets the base recording fee at five dollars for page one. Ask the Comal County Clerk, or the Guadalupe County Clerk if your parcel is there, for the current schedule.

faqs.q: How fast can a New Braunfels sale close?
faqs.a: Often in a few weeks if the title is clear. A shared inheritance, a lien or a tenant adds time. Request the closing date in writing with the offer.

faqs.q: Is New Braunfels in Comal or Guadalupe County?
faqs.a: Both. The city is the Comal County seat and extends into Guadalupe County, per the Handbook of Texas. Your tax bill shows which county's appraisal district applies.

faqs.q: How pricey is a typical New Braunfels house?
faqs.a: QuickFacts reports $339,400 as the median for owner-held homes from 2020 to 2024. Your own house's price depends on condition, location and size, so treat the figure as context only.

faqs.q: Can I sell a New Braunfels house with foundation or roof problems?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers take on the repairs themselves, and the offer accounts for them. Compare it with a repaired listing estimate to see which nets more.

faqs.q: When are New Braunfels property tax protests due?
faqs.a: Mid-May in most cases under the state calendar. The Comal Appraisal District site highlights April 15 and May 15 as key dates.
